invariants.label: Opacity Gradient
invariants.statement: Opacity is a continuous parameter ω ∈ [0,1]. Binary opacity assignments (fully opaque / fully transparent) are special cases at the interval endpoints, not a separate model.
invariants.corollary: No structure is categorically opaque or transparent in the binary sense; all assignments implicitly claim a position on the gradient.
invariants.violation: Assigning opacity as a boolean; assigning ω < 0 or ω > 1; treating binary opacity as a distinct ontological category.

invariants.label: Revelation Threshold
invariants.statement: Revelation occurs when and only when observer detection capacity δ strictly exceeds the structure's opacity value ω. At the boundary (δ = ω), the structure is treated as opaque by default.
invariants.corollary: The threshold case (δ = ω) is assigned to the opaque state by the conservatism principle. Revelation is never inferred from equal capacity and opacity.
invariants.violation: Declaring revelation when δ ≤ ω; treating the threshold case as revealed; using δ ≥ ω as the revelation condition.

invariants.label: Opacity Persistence
invariants.statement: A structure's opacity value ω is a property of its configuration, not of any observer's state. Observation does not change ω.
invariants.formal: ω(S) is invariant under change of observer O and under observation events
invariants.corollary: Multiple observers with different δ values may reach different revelation states for the same structure. This does not imply ω differs; only δ differs.
invariants.violation: Assigning or modifying ω based on observer identity, observer capacity, observation events, or observer count.

invariants.label: Partial Revelation
invariants.statement: Revelation may be partial. Not all sub-structures of a system need reveal simultaneously. The revelation state of each sub-structure s_i is evaluated independently against the observer's δ.
invariants.corollary: A structure with heterogeneous sub-structure opacity values will exhibit a partial revelation state when δ falls between the minimum and maximum opacity values of its sub-structures.
invariants.violation: Treating a structure as fully revealed because at least one sub-structure is revealed; treating it as fully opaque because at least one sub-structure remains opaque.
